evals.prompt: We need finance and legal to approve in parallel, then the CFO after both. How do I build that?
evals.expected_output: Flow-based approval workflow design using real Approval Settings and step configuration.
assertions: Designs the chain with approval workflow flows rather than classic Approval Processes.
References real Approval Settings toggles by their actual labels.
Explains step-level configuration for parallel then sequential approval.
Does not invent setting names that are not on the Approval Settings page.

evals.prompt: Can approvals skip a step when the same approver already approved a similar record? How is that configured?
evals.expected_output: Smart Approval is configured per step (Use Smart Approval plus skip conditions), not as an org-wide toggle.
assertions: States Smart Approval is configured per approval step, not as a single org-wide toggle.
Names the per-step settings (Use Smart Approval and Smart Approval Skip Conditions).
Does not invent an org-level Smart Approval lookback setting.
Mentions the documented eligibility conditions rather than guessing.

evals.prompt: An approval has been sitting unassigned for two days. Where do I look?
evals.expected_output: Queries ApprovalSubmission/ApprovalWorkItem with real status values and checks delegation, queue membership, sharing.
assertions: Inspects ApprovalSubmission and ApprovalWorkItem records.

Uses real status values -- ApprovalSubmission.Status (Approved, Canceled, Errored, InProgress, Recalled, Rejected, Suspended) and ApprovalWorkItem.Status (Assigned, Approved, Canceled, Errored, Recalled, Rejected, Withdrawn) -- rather than invented ones, and does not mix the two objects' picklists.
Checks delegation (ApprovalDelegation) and queue membership as causes.
Mentions ApprovalWorkItem record access or sharing as a cause of invisible work items.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval. Margin below 15% needs Finance. Payment terms over 60 days needs Finance too. Started by a Submit button. Use Smart Approval. Generate files only.
evals.expected_output: Runs Pre-Flight without asking about combining Finance; adds a one-line plan note instead.
assertions: Does not ask whether to combine the repeated Finance approver into one task.
Adds a one-line plan note that Finance gets 2 separate tasks and the user can say combine.
Asks which Finance queue to use instead of only asking the assignee type.
Does not ask questions the request already answers (approval type, object, how it starts, Smart Approval, scope).

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval. Margin below 15% needs Finance. Payment terms over 60 days needs Finance too. Combine Finance into one task. Started by a Submit button. Use Smart Approval. Generate files only.
evals.expected_output: Shows the before/after picture first, then asks only what is left open.
assertions: Shows a before/after picture using Finance and the user's two reasons before any row 12 question.
States, without asking, that one Finance reject rejects the quote whatever the reason.
Does not ask about chain order when Finance is the only or first approver.
Warns that the combined step gets one chain name so earlier Smart Approval history does not carry over.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval for margin below 15% needing Finance, started by a Submit button, with Smart Approval. Write the final result to the quote. Generate files only.
evals.expected_output: Uses the standard Status field and its existing values; does not invent Auto-Approved.
assertions: Uses the standard Quote Status field, after looking up its existing values in the org.
Offers only values that exist on the field, such as Approved and Rejected.
Does not offer or add an Auto-Approved value because the request never mentioned it.
Proposes a custom status field only if the object has no standard one.

evals.prompt: Create and deploy a new Advanced Approval process named TestApprprovalProcess_12 on Quote. Do not modify existing processes. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Detects that the named process already exists and asks before deploying.
assertions: Looks up whether a flow with the requested name already exists before building.
Says deploying under the existing name would add a new version and change the existing process.
Offers the next free name as the recommended option, plus new version of the existing one and another name.
Does not deploy under the existing name without the user's answer.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval for Finance, started by a Submit button, deploy and test. Use new components only if existing ones do not fit.
evals.expected_output: Looks up existing submit button, starter, gather and outcome components and judges fit before asking.
assertions: Searches the org and project, read-only, for existing quick actions, starter flow or Apex, gather subflow and outcome subflow.
Lists up to 5 closest candidates per type and says how many more exist when there are more than 2.
Treats a component hard-coded to another approval chain or status field as not fitting.
Proposes names for new components using one convention and checks them for collisions.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval: Manager for level 1 and up, Director for level 2 and up, VP for level 3 and up, plus Legal and Finance approvals triggered only by their own checkboxes. Serial. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Shows the stage layout explanation before asking the stage layout question; states the cumulative-level reading.
assertions: Shows the single-stage versus multi-stage explanation as plain text before asking the layout question.
Recommends single stage and says what multi-stage changes.
States the cumulative reading of the level matrix (level 2 means Manager then Director) or asks when unclear.
Makes Legal and Finance trigger from their checkboxes only, independent of the level.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval: Manager for level 1 and up, Director for level 2 and up, VP for level 3 and up, plus Legal and Finance triggered only by their own checkboxes. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: After the required questions, reviews the other rows in grouped prompts, never one big block.
assertions: Asks the required rows first (Legal/Finance placement, how the approval starts, level routing, status writes).
Then shows Options at a Glance as separate prompts grouped by theme (who approves; reuse and status; what people see; build), each with at most 4 rows.
Each row is a pick-one question with the recommended value first and the alternatives after it.
Rows 5, 14, 15, 16 and 17 appear even though the request did not mention them, each with its default.
Does not write any file or deploy until the groups are answered.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval with a Manager, Director and VP level chain plus Legal and Finance approvals triggered only by their checkboxes. Smart Approval on. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Recommends per-kind chain names derived from the design, not one fixed name.
assertions: Proposes one chain name for the level steps and a separate name for each other kind (Legal, Finance), named from the user's own words.
Shows which steps use each name.
Recommends one shared name only when the design has a single kind of approval.
Lets the user pick one name for all steps or type their own names.
Does not derive a chain name from the flow API name.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval for Finance started by a Submit button. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Asks for status writes per event and writes only what the user chose.
assertions: Asks about status writes at submit, when approved, when rejected, and when nothing is required.
Looks up the status field's existing values and lists them in the question.
Never writes a status the user did not choose and never hard-codes Approved or Rejected.
If a value is chosen for submit, adds a background step in the gather stage; if no write is chosen for an event, builds no stage for it.
Passes the user's value to one shared status subflow.

evals.prompt: Create and deploy a Quote approval for Legal and Finance. Use new components.
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only Environment check before the questions.
assertions: Checks that Advanced Approvals is available (the ApprovalSubmission object exists) before asking anything.
Reads the org API version and uses it for generated flows and classes.
Checks proposed component names for collisions and proposes the next free name instead of overwriting.
Does these checks read-only, without writing or deploying.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval where Legal approval is required when the Legal checkbox is true and Finance when the Finance checkbox is true. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Looks the fields up and offers to create only the missing ones with field access.
assertions: Looks the fields up in the org before trusting the names in the request.
Asks (row 18) before creating a missing field, with proposed API names, types and labels.
Creates a permission set granting field access and assigns it to the deploying user.
Deploys fields and the permission set before the other components.
Does not create a field that already exists.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval with Manager and Director steps. Use public groups as approvers, new components only. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Builds public groups correctly and orders the deploy.
assertions: Creates Group metadata with only a name element and no doesIncludeBossSubordinates.
Takes the developer name from the file name and writes the label with spaces.
Deploys the groups before the ApprovalWorkflow.
Uses assigneeType Group with the developer name in each step.
Tells the user new groups have no members so UI users see no tasks until members are added.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval for Finance. Approvers should see the quote name, total and discount on the decision screen. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Offers a custom approver screen flow with the documented contract.
assertions: Asks standard approval screen versus custom screen flow because the request mentions what approvers see.
For a custom screen flow, exposes a text output approvalDecision with Approve or Reject.
Keeps the screen to decision information and puts any other action in a background step.
Deploys the screen flow before the ApprovalWorkflow and passes recordId to it.
Offers the standard screen as the default when the request does not mention it.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval for Finance with Smart Approval on. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Treats Smart Approval as chosen but still shows the finer options.
assertions: Does not ask whether to use Smart Approval, since the request states it.
Still shows the finer choices in the grouped prompts: reuse unchanged approvals, ignore chosen start conditions, always approve again, custom comparison logic as advanced.
Builds no custom Apex auto-approval unless the user picks it.
Notes that the skip-conditions XML input name must be read from a step saved in Flow Builder.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval routed by the existing Quote.RLM_Approval_Level__c field, with Legal and Finance by checkbox. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Describes the existing level field and handles a calculated field before creating test data.
assertions: Describes RLM_Approval_Level__c and reads createable, updateable and calculated before using it.

If the field is calculated or not updateable, says a permission set cannot make it writable and asks (row 18): another field, a new writable field, driving the calculated field, or skipping runtime tests.
Does not try to create test quotes that set a calculated field.
If the field is writable but the user lacks edit access, adds it to the permission set without changing the field.
Creates only the checkbox fields that are missing and never recreates an existing field.

evals.prompt: Build a Quote approval with Legal and Finance checkboxes that do not exist yet in the org. Deploy and test.
evals.expected_output: Asks about the field access permission set instead of assuming one.
assertions: Looks up which permission sets already grant edit on the routing fields before proposing anything.
Asks (row 19) whether to create a new permission set, add the fields to an existing one the user picks, or make no change.
Warns that editing an existing permission set changes access for every user of it.
Asks who should be assigned: the deploying user only, named users, or a permission set group.
Does not edit an existing permission set unless the user chose it.
